## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><b>Header</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What do you read first?">Hierarchy</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="What belongs together?">Grouping</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">What is the main content? → Numbers and records</div><div class="odv-am-why">Most of the screen is numbers and records.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · Which text roles does it need? → Core and data</div><div class="odv-am-why">A data role keeps numbers in aligned columns.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For field label or column header, use type.label. Don't use type.heading.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Headers repeat on every column; a heavy style would compete with the data.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.sunken</code><span>→</span><code>header-background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#EEF1F5 · dark #262D38</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.sunken.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.text.secondary</code><span>→</span><code>head.label</code><span class="odv-am-val">#3D4655 · dark #C4CBD6</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">Supporting text.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.700: supporting text, 9.52:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.500: supporting text, 10.58:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>type.label.font-weight</code><span>→</span><code>head.font-weight</code><span class="odv-am-val">500</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> font.weight.500</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>space.inset.cell-x</code><span>→</span><code>head.padding-x</code><span class="odv-am-val">0.75rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. <section class="odv-am-card" id="part-3-4"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><i class="odv-am-n">4</i><b>Row</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you hit it?">Reach</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">How much is on one screen? → A lot</div><div class="odv-am-why">Experts want many records on one screen.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Compact</div><div class="odv-am-why">Compact spacing shows more records.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For table row height, use size.row (compact). ## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `table`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data table`
